title: Basic Prompt Injection (HelperBot)
summary: As documented, the attacker replaces the agent's instructions and can direct it to do things it was not designed to do. As implemented, the effect is an acknowledgement string.

LC.rationale: In the documented default simulated configuration no model is called, and the HelperBot handler answers the override payload with a fixed acknowledgement; later requests are unchanged, so attacker language never reaches a privileged decision or tool sink.

CP.rationale: Memory persistence is described only for MemoryBot; other chat agents, including this path, answer only the latest user turn and do not carry attacker context across requests.

AP.rationale: The scored effect is HelperBot's own reply string. A2A handoffs are declared but not implemented, and this path does not call another agent, tenant, or policy domain.

RH.rationale: The in-repo check is an external unit test of the acknowledgement string and is not an agent-reachable evaluator; the packet has no verified reward-hacking episode and no test that reward channels are isolated.

ES.rationale: HelperBot lists tool names, but default chat handling does not pass tools to a model, and only separate scripted paths execute anything; this path returns a constant string.

agentic_applicability.rationale: The challenge documents the agent as accepting and following replaced instructions and as directable to undesigned actions, and the HelperBot persona declares read_file, write_file, and search_web.
